panels.rationale: Caption explicitly attributes bilateral plantar hyperkeratosis to acrokeratosis paraneoplastica in article titled Acrokeratosis Paraneoplastica Associated with Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma, matching configured disease and fissured palmoplantar keratoderma finding visible as diffuse plantar scaling/hyperkeratosis.

panels.figure_caption: Acrokeratosis paraneoplastica. The bilateral plantar feet demonstrated hyperkeratosis extending to the lateral surfaces of the feet and toes.
in_text_mentions: Physical exam revealed scaly hyperpigmented plaques on the ulnar surfaces of the bilateral hands and the periungual skin of the fingers, with some fissuring. There was irregular pitting of the right fifth fingernails (Figure 1). The bilateral plantar feet demonstrated hyperkeratosis extending to the lateral surfaces of the feet and toes (Figure 2). Xerotic scaling and excoriations were present on the bilateral upper arms, lower legs, and lower back. The xerosis was accentuated on the lower legs with fine, polygonal cracks (Figure 3).

plate_findings.evidence: Hands showing symmetrical psoriasiform lesions bilaterally.
Nails were thickened with dystrophic thickening

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left dorsal hand view of disease-focused article on Acrokeratosis Paraneoplastica with captioned symmetrical psoriasiform lesions and in-text nail dystrophy/subungual hyperkeratosis; shows symmetric acral hyperkeratotic plaques. B: Right palmar hand view of same hands with symmetric psoriasiform/hyperkeratotic lesions and dystrophic nails, supporting acrokeratosis paraneoplastica attribution per caption and disease-focused title.
